answer: Ephemeral beacon island mapping. Each epoch, a public randomness beacon assigns every agent a temporary island (a shard); only agents on the same island can transact that epoch. An identity survives into the next epoch only if its island relic—a shard-signed receipt of real activity—is co-signed by a random quorum drawn from that island. Because the beacon output is unknowable before the epoch opens, attackers cannot pre-place sock puppets on the island where their target lands.
